html:
In September 1807 a British fleet and army bombarded Copenhagen for three nights, then seized the whole Danish navy so that it could not fall into French hands.

Denmark was neutral, but Britain feared Napoleon would force it to hand over its fleet. The city was hit by Congreve rockets and set on fire. Many civilians died and much of the old town burned.

Denmark then allied with France. It lost the war that followed, and in 1814 the Treaty of Kiel gave Norway to Sweden, ending Denmark-Norway after more than four centuries. The attack was one of the first on a capital aimed at its civilians, and it left Denmark a small, poor state. See the Napoleonic Wars.
sum: In September 1807 a British fleet and army bombarded Copenhagen for three nights, then seized the whole Danish navy so that it could not fall into French hands.
